title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ（平田宏聡研究室）
subtitle: Design Project III(Hirata Hiroaki)
educationalGoal: Spatiotemporal control of cells underlies structures and functions of our bodies. Our laboratory studies how cellular functions are regulated by intracellular and extracellular mechanical environments. Furthermore, we aim at developing a new medical strategy for the cell function control by mechanical intervention. By conducting these researches, students will learn experimental/analytical skills in cell biology and mechanobiology, and acquire skills for scientific thinking.
advice:
Specific research themes will be determined based on students’ interests and discussion with the supervisor.
In prior to conducting experiments and analyses, students need to prepare their detailed plans.
We will have weekly lab meetings for progress reports and journal club.
Logical thinking, which is essential for planning experiments/analyses and deriving conclusion from obtained results in any R&D activities, will be trained by active discussion in lab meetings.
requiredKnowledge:
Basic knowledge of cell biology, molecular biology and biochemistry is required.
Students are encouraged to actively introduce new experimental/analytical methods into their own projects.

activityGoals.body: Ability to accumulate and explain background knowledge required for conducting research
Ability to logically approach issues yet to be revealed
Ability to plan and conduct experiments/analyses, and discuss the results
Ability to describe cellular functions from the aspect of integration of biochemical and mechanical information
Ability to report and present clearly the research achievement

●Propose a reasonable research theme based on extensive survey of previous studies
●Prepare detailed and reasonable plans for experiments/analyses
●Conduct experiments/analyses in correct ways
●Integrate multiple results to derive a conclusion
●Report and present the research achievement logically and clearly
achievementLevels.standard:
●Survey and understand previous studies related to the research theme
●Prepare and modify plans for experiments/analyses
●Conduct experiments/analyses in correct ways
●Derive a conclusion from each result
●Report and present the research achievement logically

              Spatiotemporal control of cells underlies structures and functions of our bodies. Our laboratory studies how cellular functions are regulated by intracellular and extracellular mechanical environments. Furthermore, we aim at developing a new medical strategy for the cell function control by mechanical intervention. By conducting these researches, students will learn experimental/analytical skills in cell biology and mechanobiology, and acquire skills for scientific thinking.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              Specific research themes will be determined based on students’ interests and discussion with the supervisor.
In prior to conducting experiments and analyses, students need to prepare their detailed plans.
We will have weekly lab meetings for progress reports and journal club.
Logical thinking, which is essential for planning experiments/analyses and deriving conclusion from obtained results in any R&D activities, will be trained by active discussion in lab meetings.
